'''Auyokawa''' (Auyo), also known as '''Tirio''', is an extinct [[Afro-Asiatic languages|Afro-Asiatic]] language formerly spoken in [[Auyo]] LGA, [[Jigawa State]], [[Nigeria]].<ref name="e16">{{Ethnologue16|auo|Auyokawa}} </ref><ref name="BlenchAtlas4">{{Cite book|title=An Atlas of Nigerian Languages|last=Blench|first=Roger|publisher=Kay Williamson Educational Foundation|year=2019|edition=4th|location=Cambridge}}</ref> It is known primarily from a list of numbers, the names of the days of the week, and a phrase.<ref name=":0">{{Citation |last=Schuh |first=Russell G. |title=Shira, Teshena, Auyo: Hausa's (former) eastern neighbors |date=2001 |work=Historical Language Contact in Africa |volume=16/17 |pages=387–435 <!--|url= |access-date=2025-05-25 --> |series=Sprache und Geschichte in Afrika |place=Köln |publisher=Rüdiger Köppe}}</ref>
